author: original (NevaIB)
title: Rational exponents, laws of logarithms and exponential equations

points.text: Product, quotient and power laws of logarithms
Changing the base of a logarithm
Solving exponential equations, including by taking logs

bigPicture: With fractional powers and the log laws you can rearrange and solve almost any exponential equation. Paper 1 tests the exact algebra; Paper 2 lets the GDC check it.

keyIdeas.answer: The nth root of a, raised to the power m: (ⁿ√a)^m.
log(xy) = log x + log y; log(x/y) = log x − log y; log(x^m) = m log x (same base throughout).
log_a x = log_b x / log_b a, for any base b, e.g. ln x / ln a.
Take logs: x ln 5 = ln 12, so x = ln 12 / ln 5.

keyTerms.def: rewriting a log in a different base by dividing two logs

misconceptions.wrong: log(x + y) = log x + log y
misconceptions.right: No such law; only log(xy) splits into a sum.
The power law applies to log(x²), not to the log squared.

practice.prompt: £2000 grows as 2000(1.035)^t. Find t when the value first exceeds £3000.
solution: first exceeds after 12 whole years if compounded yearly
commonErrors: Answering 11 when the context needs whole years

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.
